b: The Fraser River on Canada’s west coast province of British Columbia is arguably the best place on the planet to catch-and-release oversize white sturgeon. The giant fish are protected by law for harvest, but catch-and-release fishing is allowed.
Among the many guide operations that target Fraser River sturgeon for clients, Sturgeon Slayers is consistently one of the best for producing fish in the half-ton weight range.

Owned and operated by Kevin Estrada, Sturgeon Slayers guided trips have led anglers to catch several record-size white sturgeon in recent years. Some of those catches have been chronicled in Wired2fish. Recently, an eye-opening catch by lady angler Katharine Eckert went unnoticed until now.

Former NHL goaltender Pete Peeters caught an estimated 890-pound Fraser River sturgeon with Estrada. It was much larger than the standing world record. But as required by law, the fish was released unharmed and never weighed.

That huge sturgeon caught by Peeters inspired Katharine Eckert, of Maplewood, Missouri (near St. Louis), to book a June sturgeon fishing trip with Estrada. She fished with him on June 10, shortly after Estrada had just led another group of male anglers to a huge fish.
On June 4 Estrada guided those anglers to a record length 11-foot, 8-inch sturgeon estimated at 1,200 pounds. It had a 60.23-inch girth and was widely covered by news media, including Wired2fish.

Just a week later, Eckert made her fishing trip with Estrada and after a 40-minute fight, caught a giant 11-foot, 4-inch sturgeon, while fishing the Fraser River near the town of Chilliwack. Not until now has news of Eckert’s remarkable sturgeon catch been made known.

“There was so much publicity around the 1,200-pounder that those men caught, that we pretty much kept it quiet about Katharine’s equally impressive catch,” said Estrada. “But it’s time to let the word out on her huge sturgeon, which may be the world record for weight of a freshwater fish.”

Eckert’s sturgeon could not be officially weighed because of strict catch-and-release restrictions on angling for the rare species. Estrada is a widely acknowledged authority on white sturgeon and does extensive work with biologists studying the species. He’s guided anglers to many huge fish and has handled plenty of big ones.

Estrada says Eckert’s sturgeon was as big as any he has seen. And he can find no record of a freshwater fish caught by any woman larger than her estimated 1,200 pounder – that was tagged and released back into the river after her catch.
Sturgeon Don’t Grow Much Larger Than This
“Katharine’s sturgeon was just as fat as the longer fish caught a week earlier by the men,” Estrada said. “It measured 60 inches of girth around the pectoral fins, 70 inches at the belly.

“It never jumped because she caught it in very shallow water, and they need a little deeper water to get airborne. It came up and rolled at the surface and fought her tough on heavy tackle that included a 9-foot rod, 200-pound-test braided line, doubled 70-pound-test leaders, and a 10/0 hook.”

No live bait is allowed for sturgeon on the Fraser, and Estrada won’t reveal the secret bait he uses for his fishing clients. “There are just some things I’m not going to reveal – and our sturgeon bait is one of them,” he said with a chuckle.
